zh.title: 國籍航空國際航線燃油附加費9月7日調漲 短程1028元長程2670元
zh.summary: 民航局宣布9月7日起調漲國籍航空國際線燃油附加費；短程1028元長程2670元
body: 交通部民用航空局於9月1日宣布，由於國際航空燃油價格近期上漲，國籍航空公司國際航線客運燃油附加費將自9月7日起實施調漲。
根據民航局規範，短程航線燃油附加費將從原先的30美元（約新台幣949元）調漲至32.5美元（約新台幣1028元）；長程航線燃油附加費則由原先的78美元（約新台幣2467元）調漲至84.5美元（約新台幣2670元）。短程航線範圍為亞洲（不含印度與中東），長程航線範圍為歐洲、美洲、非洲、大洋洲、南極洲、印度與中東。
本次燃油附加費調漲係依據台灣中油公司公告之國際航空燃油價格。中油公告牌價由每桶147.57美元（約新台幣4668元）調漲至每桶156.79美元（約新台幣4960元），帶動附加費依機制向上調整。

民航局於2005年與國籍航空公司協調建立客運燃油附加費調整機制，以中油公司公告之國際航空燃油每桶牌價為收取基準。當油價未達每桶40美元（約新台幣1265元）時為不收費級距；達40美元至未滿50美元（約新台幣1581元）為起徵第2級距，短程線每人收取5美元（約新台幣158元），長程線每人收取13美元（約新台幣411元）。油價每增加10美元（約新台幣316元），短程線增加2.5美元（約新台幣79元），長程線增加6.5美元（約新台幣206元）。
民航局表示，已要求各航空公司應以適當方式揭露相關背景資訊，例如燃油成本占總成本比例或計算方式等，以化解消費者疑慮。旅客亦可洽各航空公司或至其官網查詢相關調整資訊。

en.title: Taiwan CAA Increases Fuel Surcharges for International Flights from Sept 7
en.summary: Taiwan CAA announced international passenger fuel surcharges for domestic carriers will increase starting September 7.
body: Taiwan's Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA) announced on September 1 that international passenger fuel surcharges for domestic airlines will be increased starting September 7, driven by recent increases in international aviation fuel prices.

According to the CAA, short-haul fuel surcharges will increase from $30 USD (approximately NT$949) to $32.50 USD (approximately NT$1,028) per passenger. Long-haul fuel surcharges will rise from $78 USD (approximately NT$2,467) to $84.50 USD (approximately NT$2,670) per passenger. Short-haul routes cover Asia excluding India and the Middle East, while long-haul routes encompass Europe, the Americas, Africa, Oceania, Antarctica, India, and the Middle East.

The surcharge rate adjustment is based on the latest international aviation fuel prices announced by CPC Corporation. The listed price for international jet fuel increased from $147.57 USD (approximately NT$4,668) per barrel to $156.79 USD (approximately NT$4,960) per barrel, triggering the automatic bracket step-up under the mechanism.

The CAA established the passenger fuel surcharge adjustment mechanism in 2005 through coordination with domestic airlines, using CPC Corporation's announced international aviation fuel list price as the baseline standard. Under the agreement, no surcharge is collected when fuel prices remain below $40 USD (approximately NT$1,265) per barrel. The second tier begins between $40 USD and under $50 USD (approximately NT$1,581) per barrel, with charges set at $5 USD (approximately NT$158) for short-haul and $13 USD (approximately NT$411) for long-haul flights. For each subsequent $10 USD (approximately NT$316) increase in fuel price, short-haul and long-haul surcharges increase by $2.50 USD (approximately NT$79) and $6.50 USD (approximately NT$206), respectively.

The CAA added that it has instructed airlines to appropriately disclose background information, such as the proportion of fuel costs relative to total operating costs or calculation formulas, to resolve consumer inquiries. Passengers can also contact individual airlines or check official websites for details regarding the upcoming adjustment.
